top3.headline: A poisoned LiteLLM release on PyPI installs a credential stealer
top3.whyItMatters: Any machine that installed version 1.107.0 should be treated as compromised and its keys rotated.

top3.headline: Claude stops asking permission at each step by default next week
top3.whyItMatters: Agents acting on their own becomes the default for paying users, so set governance first.

top3.headline: The full Claude Platform is now generally available on Google Cloud
top3.whyItMatters: With OpenAI models also coming to Google Cloud, model choice no longer forces a cloud choice.

items.title: Rauch: replace static credentials with short-lived keys, like the TLS push
items.takeaway: Guillermo Rauch calls for the industry to kill static credentials and move to short-lived, self-destructing keys via OIDC, comparing it to the push for TLS.
items.soWhat: Ask which of your systems still run on long-lived keys, and set a date to retire them.

items.title: Hermes agents get their own computers that teammates can take over
items.takeaway: A new trycua Spaces plugin gives Nous Research's Hermes its own Linux, macOS or Windows Space on hardware you own. Teammates can watch live, step in and hand it back.
items.soWhat: Human takeover of a running agent is becoming a built-in feature, not a custom build.

items.title: Anthropic uses Claude to formally verify software at large scale
items.takeaway: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team describes using Claude to formally verify software at large scale, work once feasible only for small codebases or with a lot of expert time.
items.soWhat: Proving critical code correct could move from rare expert work to a routine engineering step.

items.title: Full Claude Platform now generally available inside Google Cloud
items.takeaway: Claude Models on Google Cloud, managed by Anthropic, is generally available with Google Cloud IAM, billing and commitment retirement, including Claude Managed Agents, code execution and Opus 5.5 fast mode.
items.soWhat: Existing Google Cloud commitments can now pay for Claude, so procurement is no longer the blocker.

items.title: Perplexity adds batch runs of up to 50,000 agent requests
items.takeaway: Perplexity's Agent API now has a Batch API supporting up to 50k requests per file. Each request runs the full agent loop with web search and page fetch.
items.soWhat: Large research tasks can now run as one scheduled agent batch instead of thousands of calls.

items.title: Claude will act without step-by-step approval by default next week
items.takeaway: From next week, Claude web, desktop and mobile sessions on Pro, Max and Team run in auto mode by default. An automated check blocks risky actions; users can switch back to manual.
items.soWhat: Set your team's Claude policy before the default flips, not after the first surprise action.

items.title: Microsoft's diagnostic AI shows higher accuracy at lower cost in Science
items.takeaway: Microsoft published work in Science showing its diagnostic orchestrator reaching greater accuracy at lower testing cost on complex cases. Microsoft claims up to four times better than doctors.
items.soWhat: Peer-reviewed results move clinical AI from demo to procurement conversation for health leaders.

items.title: OpenAI launches a Decisions API for fast, low-cost choices
items.takeaway: OpenAI launched the Decisions API, pitched as fast, focused, low-cost decisions for any application.
items.soWhat: Ask your teams which routine yes-or-no calls in your apps could move to it.

items.title: One prompt moves a Claude or Codex site into Framer
items.takeaway: Meng To shows the Framer MCP turning Claude and Codex sites into Framer sites with one prompt: 'Create a copy of this site in Framer using the MCP'.
items.soWhat: Prototypes built by AI can now land in a tool your designers already edit.

items.title: Andreessen sees the widest AI gap yet between startups and incumbents
items.takeaway: Marc Andreessen says the gap between what AI-native startups and incumbents think AI can do is the widest he has seen. Individuals adopt faster than organizations, often without telling management.
items.soWhat: Your people may already use AI quietly; ask what works before you write policy.

items.title: Canva launches Craft, its first in-house image model
items.takeaway: Canva Craft uses a two-stage architecture that plans a design before generating it. It is live in Dream Lab.
items.soWhat: Design platforms are building their own models instead of only renting from labs.

items.title: NVIDIA open-sources OpenShell, a private runtime for agent fleets
items.takeaway: NVIDIA open-sourced OpenShell, described as a safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents.
items.soWhat: Agent isolation is becoming open infrastructure, so you can ask for it from every vendor.

items.title: Benaich: Europe cannot rent its way to AI sovereignty
items.takeaway: Nathan Benaich argues June's US export controls showed Washington can control access without owning the labs. A domestic data center does not give control over the models inside it.
items.soWhat: Hosting AI locally is not the same as controlling it; check who can switch your models off.

items.title: Anthropic, OpenAI and Nvidia post record lobbying quarters
items.takeaway: Federal disclosures show each had its highest-spending lobbying quarter in July-September: Nvidia $2.2M, Anthropic $2.1M, OpenAI $1.5M.
items.soWhat: The labs are spending more to shape AI rules; plan for regulation written with their input.

items.title: OpenAI publishes an official command-line tool on GitHub
items.takeaway: OpenAI published an official OpenAI CLI repository on GitHub.
items.soWhat: Developers and their agents can now script OpenAI from the terminal with a vendor-supported tool.

items.title: Dalio: diagnose a hard problem before you design the fix
items.takeaway: Ray Dalio says jumping from a tough problem straight to a solution is a common mistake. Strategic thinking needs diagnosis and design; a good diagnosis takes fifteen minutes to an hour.
items.soWhat: Give your team an hour of diagnosis before any AI strategy decision.

items.title: Mistral releases Mistral Large 4
items.takeaway: Mistral released Mistral Large 4. The announcement drew 322 points on Hacker News.
items.soWhat: Mistral is a non-US frontier option; keep it in your vendor comparisons.

items.title: Agents miss highlighted requirements when documents lose their formatting
items.takeaway: On 76 real policy documents, recovering author-flagged requirements fell from F1 0.690 to 0.150 with docling. Highlight and colour carry the loss; 32.8% of 6,460 documents use them.
items.soWhat: Check how your agents ingest documents before trusting their compliance answers.

image.alt: arXiv: Agents miss highlighted requirements when documents lose their formatting

items.title: Brockman says defenders can hold the edge as agents find flaws
items.takeaway: OpenAI published Patch the Planet, on coordinating responses as agents uncover vulnerabilities. In an a16z clip, Greg Brockman discusses a $1B commitment to secure critical infrastructure.
items.soWhat: Labs now treat AI-found flaws as a coordination problem, and your patch speed is part of it.

items.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI shipped a credential stealer and backdoor
items.takeaway: SafeDep reports that LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI was compromised and installs a credential stealer and backdoor.
items.soWhat: If any team installed that version, treat its keys as stolen and rotate them today.

items.title: Meng To open-sources a skill that turns apps into HTML demos
items.takeaway: The skill makes demos that stay sharp at any size, loop, scrub, jump to any step and respect reduced motion.
items.soWhat: Product teams can build interactive demos from the app itself, without a video editor.

hotOnX.text: Starting next week, Claude web, desktop and mobile run in auto mode by default on Pro, Max and Team plans.
hotOnX.note: Default autonomy for paying users changes who approves an agent's actions.

hotOnX.text: Agent Skills goes to the Agentic AI Foundation; 70+ agent platforms have integrated it since December 2025.
hotOnX.note: A shared skill format means work done for one agent carries to others.

hotOnX.text: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed) is generally available, with Google Cloud IAM and billing.
hotOnX.note: Enterprises can buy Claude through an existing Google Cloud contract.

hotOnX.text: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team on using Claude to formally verify software at large scale.
hotOnX.note: Formal proof of code has been too costly for most teams; this tests whether that changes.

hotOnX.text: OpenAI invited METR and Redwood Research to pilot a three-week embedded evaluation of its internal monitoring.
hotOnX.note: Outside auditors with deep access is a rare test of lab safety claims.
